title: The Unique Role of Electron Microscopy in Unraveling and Mitigating Materials Sources of Decoherence in Superconducting Quantum Devices
content: Superconducting qubits have garnered significant interest in the field of quantum information science, due to their long coherence times that now reach hundreds of microseconds [1-2], pushing the field towards quantum advantage [3]. However, further insights and advances in materials science are necessary to achieve scalable, fault-tolerant quantum computers that can accelerate computing technologies beyond the classical regime. Namely, while it is widely viewed that there are sources of two-level system (TLS) and non-TLS losses residing in materials-level defects, surfaces, and interfaces in superconducting quantum circuits, an atomic-level understanding of how structure and chemistry precisely impact qubit coherence remains limited, thus presenting significant challenges to achieving even greater performance levels [4-7]. Implementation of decoherence-mitigation strategies in device fabrication, architecture development, and error correction—all critical for demonstration of quantum advantage—rely heavily on elucidating the primary coherence-limiting materials-level loss sources and channels.
